non_blocking.suggestion: By the manifest word_count_rule (prose after front matter, fenced code excluded) the body has about 1,499 words, against the adr_common maximum of 1,500. Any further edit must cost no words. Mermaid labels are free, so fixes to Figure 1 do not count against the band. Do not delete text that resolved L2-1 to L2-7.

"It matches foundation pack section 7 and the [Library catalog]" overstates the match. The catalog row reads "Ruralz Control and CLI import only `ast` and `astvalidation`", while this ADR's `ruralz-control`, `ruralz` row adds the lexer, parser, normalization and `engine/plan`. The More information amendment already covers the change. Make the sentence word-neutral: "It matches foundation pack section 7; the [Library catalog] row changes as proposed below."

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (`ruralz-control`, `ruralz` row, line 49); More information
non_blocking.suggestion: The spike "planning without transports" has no fallback. If `engine/plan` turns out to need `graphql_datasource` federation configuration, or transitively links `engine/resolve` (see L1-1), the "never `engine/resolve`" rule and the Review checklist set would both need to change. Name the fallback that keeps the Configuration model validation contract. For example: widen the linked set to the datasource configuration packages, still without transports or `subscription`, and amend the depguard rule. Do not accept a sixth post-offline failure.

non_blocking.section: Decision drivers (Runtime configuration, line 27); More information (OQ-multi-protocol-4 amendment, line 146)
non_blocking.suggestion: Offline `ruralz bundle validate` can plan against the supergraph only if its SDL is Bundle content. "Offline validation needs no registry" in the Configuration model rules out a registry fetch there. If OQ-multi-protocol-4 option (c) instead fetches an external artifact by digest, the planning check becomes an online check like RZ-CFG-028. Add to the existing OQ-multi-protocol-4 amendment that the pinned SDL must be readable offline from the Bundle, or else register an online check through the Configuration model. Name no field.

Figure 1 has 16 nodes and mermaid labels are outside the word count. Adding `onRoute` (once per operation) and `onChunk` per resolved event on the subscription path would complete "where each operation meets the Filter Chain" for the owning document's GraphQL columns. Figure 1 also sends pass-through from `lim` straight to `leg`, so it shows no component that opens the upstream `graphql-transport-ws` for a pass-through subscription (see L1-2). Label that edge with its transport or its Open question.

The driver lists S1 to S4, S6 and S7 but leaves out S5 ("Protocol completeness (federation, KIP coverage, MQTT v5)"). S5 is the criterion federation versions 1 and 2 answer, and the Protocol conformance suite confirms it. Write "S1 to S7" in place of "S1 to S4, S6 and S7", which saves words.

non_blocking.section: Confirmation (G1, G3 and license gate, line 101)
non_blocking.suggestion: "Go-module-only cryptography" does not use the tech stack's G3 wording and could be read as any Go module. G3 reads "Cryptographic primitives come only from Go `crypto/...` or from `golang.org/x/crypto` packages that delegate to the Go Cryptographic Module". Write "cryptography only via the Go Cryptographic Module".

"so a Revision's schema would need a rebuild" presumes that a Revision carries a GraphQL schema. The Configuration model does not define one yet (OQ-multi-protocol-4). Use the hedged wording from line 27: "so a schema change would need a rebuilt binary rather than a new Revision, breaking P5".
